# 3 Maccabees Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** Ptolemy at Raphia and Jerusalem

---

**1** When Philopator learned from returning soldiers that Antiochus had seized the territories he controlled, he mobilized all his infantry and cavalry forces, took his sister Arsinoe with him, and marched toward Raphia, where Antiochus and his army were camped.

**2** But a man named Theodotus, plotting treachery, took the finest weapons that had been entrusted to him and slipped into Ptolemy's tent at night, intending to assassinate the king single-handedly and end the war.

**3** However, Dositheus, known as the son of Drimylus, a Jewish man by birth who had later abandoned his religion and ancestral customs, quietly moved the king out of the tent and arranged for a worthless nobody to sleep there in his place. When Theodotus struck, it was that man he killed instead.

**4** A fierce battle was fought, and things were looking favorable for Philopator. Antiochus could see that the situation was deteriorating for his side.

**5** He pulled back in order to reorganize his forces.

**6** After the battle, Ptolemy reviewed his troops and went from city to city, encouraging the populations and lifting morale.

**7** In the course of this tour he came to Judea and to Jerusalem, where he offered sacrifice to the Most High God in a manner befitting the occasion.

**8** He made thank-offerings, performed the proper rites for the holy place, and then entered the outer court. He was immediately struck with admiration at its orderliness and beauty.

**9** He was so impressed by the arrangement of the temple that he conceived a desire to enter the inner sanctuary.

**10** When they told him this was not permitted, that even the priests could not enter there, and that the high priest himself only entered once a year and alone, Ptolemy refused to accept this.

**11** Even when the written law was read to him, he would not back down. He said: Even if that rule applies to them, it should not apply to me.

**12** He argued: I have entered the temples of all the other peoples, and none of their priests stopped me at the door.

**13** Someone rebuked him for this, pointing out that such pride was misplaced.

**14** But he pressed on toward the inner sanctuary regardless, and in response the priests threw themselves down together with all the people, begging him to turn back from this act of sacrilege.

**15** The city was thrown into an uproar. The priests in their vestments prostrated themselves before the altar and called out to heaven in urgent prayer for help in this crisis.

**16** Their cries were heard, and the whole city was filled with weeping and lamentation.

**17** People poured out of their houses and crowded toward the heart-wrenching scene of mass supplication.

**18** Women had shut themselves in with their children and locked their doors; some leaned out from windows, others from rooftops, stretching their hands toward heaven and crying out in desperate prayer.

**19** It was a heartbreaking sight: the whole multitude prostrate in prayer, and the anguish of the high priest visible in his distress.

**20** As they pleaded and prayed, calling on the Almighty Lord to come to their aid in this critical moment, the high priest Shimon prostrated himself before the sanctuary and prayed these words.

**21** O Lord, Lord, King of the heavens and Master of all creation, Holy One among the holy ones, sole Ruler, Almighty, hear us who are weighed down by the wickedness of this impure man, this arrogant, power-drunk tyrant.

**22** You who created everything and govern the whole world are a righteous Judge, and you pass judgment on those who act with violence and arrogance.

**23** You destroyed the lawbreakers of former times, including the giants who put their confidence in their own strength and boldness, upon whom you brought destruction without limit.

**24** You made the Sodomites who lived without law a notorious example for all generations after them.

**25** You showed your great power to the arrogant Pharaoh who had enslaved your holy people Israel, afflicting them with every kind of severe suffering.

**26** When he pursued them with chariots and a great army, you drowned him in the depths of the sea, while those who had put their trust in you, the Ruler of all creation, passed through safely.

**27** When they had seen your mighty works, they praised you, the Almighty.

**28** You, O King, when you created this immeasurable earth, chose this city and consecrated this place for the glory of your name, though you need nothing from us. You glorified it with your magnificent presence and established it as the firm foundation for the honor of your great and holy name.

**29** And loving the house of Israel, you promised that if we fell away and trouble came upon us, if we came to this place and prayed, you would hear our prayer.

**30** And you are faithful and true.
